author: ValWood
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**


GO:0048254 | snoRNA localization | IBA with PTN001782010 , Q9NWK9


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC4F10.19c

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

This isn't totally incorrect, because the protein is involved in 
box C/D snoRNP assembly
and a consequence of mutation is mislocalization.
But I feel that it  is more of a phenotype than a process  (but that goes for pretty much all localization that isn't active transport, I only have a small number of exceptions).

...anyway in general I think we should probably avoid "localization" as a PAINTed process.
@pgaudet  do you have thoughts on this. I think we have discussed in the past....

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
title: GO:0048254	 snoRNA localization IBA with PTN001782010 , Q9NWK9

author: ValWood
body:
In this case the title of the paper the inference is from is

"A dynamic scaffold of pre-snoRNP factors facilitates human box C/D snoRNP assembly."

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Usually I do not spend much time on updating "not totally incorrect" tickets. 
But as we have the  annotation to BP assembly which looks good, I agreed to removed the localization term.
